problem: All manifolds are connected and compact. Write dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Use genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives. For a smooth real (1,1) form theta, PSH(X,theta) means theta+dd^c u>=0. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C and equivalence means mutual order, including the canonical values at common poles. Extended products mean non-pluripolar Monge-Ampere products with smooth-background corrections. A big background admits a genuine strict current theta+dd^c u>=epsilon h for some Hermitian h and epsilon>0. BMP means v_+(h)<infinity, where v_+(h) and v_-(h) are the supremum and infimum of integral(h+dd^c u)^n over all bounded h-psh u. Positive lower mass means v_-(h)>0; it is distinct from BMP. Fix a Hermitian h on a manifold of dimension n>=2 and a finite nonzero positive non-pluripolar Borel measure nu, meaning it gives zero mass to every locally pluripolar Borel set. Do not assume nu has a density against smooth volume. Original S15 asks for intrinsic individual criteria distinguishing (A) some genuine h-psh u and a>0 with MA_ext_h(u)>=a nu, (B) an exact finite-mass equation MA_ext_h(u)=c nu with c>0 and sup u=0, and (C) MA_ext_h(u)=exp(lambda u)nu for a specified lambda>0, with a natural class and any normalization correctly stated. Exponential equations are not invariant under adding constants with their scalar fixed. Known background: v_-(h)>0 is equivalent to exact solvability for every finite non-pluripolar measure in the relative envelope class E_env(X,h,0). Here E_env consists of u preceq phi such that for each t>=1 some genuine h-psh v satisfies t^(-1)v+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u; unrestricted envelope equality is not its definition. At zero lower mass even absolutely continuous probability measures bounded below by a positive constant can have no positive scaled subsolution, although every smooth density is solvable. For individual density f dV, the bounded truncation constants define b_h(f)=lim_k c_h(min(f,k)), exactly characterize positive scaled subsolutions and attain the maximal coefficient. A maximal subsolution may have excess or infinite mass, so this does not alone answer (B). General nu has no canonical bounded truncation relative to smooth volume. Existing prescribed-reference measure theorems have model, lower-volume and genuine smaller-background hypotheses. Bounded concentration obstructions do not settle unbounded exponential solvability. No replacement threshold, measure construction or proof is supplied.
completionCriteria: Give a new intrinsic and non-tautological individual criterion for general non-pluripolar nu, with complete implications for scaled subsolutions, exact finite-mass normalized equations and exponential equations distinguished precisely. A new sufficient-condition theorem must cover a substantive measure singular with respect to smooth volume and address the stated zero-lower-mass or prescribed-type obstruction beyond the known positive-lower-mass universal theorem. Do not define the criterion merely as existence of the requested subsolution, silently insert bounded-density truncations, or infer an exact finite-mass product from an attained inequality. Verify compactness, domination, canonical representatives and indispensable primary sources; independently reconstruct the full proof and retain any unresolved assertions.
